models.description:
# Model Summary

**Description**

**T5Gemma** is a family of lightweight yet powerful encoder-decoder research models from Google, built by adapting pretrained decoder-only Gemma models into encoder-decoder ones. T5Gemma 2 models, based on Gemma 3, are multilingual and multimodal, handling text and image input and generating text output, with open weights for three pretrained sizes (270M-270M, 1B-1B, and 4B-4B).

**T5Gemma 2** has promising long-context capability, supporting a 128K context window in over 140 languages. Different from T5Gemma, this series adopts tied word embeddings (over encoder and decoder) and merged decoder self- and cross-attention to save model parameters. T5Gemma 2 models are well-suited for a variety of text generation and image understanding tasks, including question answering, summarization, and reasoning. Their relatively small size makes it possible to deploy them in environments with limited resources such as laptops, desktops or your own cloud infrastructure, democratizing access to state of the art AI models and helping foster innovation for everyone.

##**Inputs and outputs**

**Input:**

  * Text string, such as a question, a prompt, or a document to be summarized
  * Images, normalized to 896 x 896 resolution and encoded to 256 tokens each
  * Total input context of 128K tokens

**Output:**

* Generated text in response to the input, such as an answer to a question, analysis of image content, or a summary of a document
* Total output context up to 32K tokens


## Links

* [T5Gemma 2 Quickstart Notebook](https://colab.sandbox.google.com/gist/laxmareddyp/5f91373b4cee625c8bc702b5a5441fb6/t5gemma2-quick-inference-on-images-and-text.ipynb)
* [T5Gemma 2 API Documentation](https://keras.io/keras_hub/api/models/t5gemma2/)
* [T5Gemma 2 Model Card](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/t5gemma-2/)
* [KerasHub Beginner Guide](https://keras.io/guides/keras_hub/getting_started/)
* [KerasHub Model Publishing Guide](https://keras.io/guides/keras_hub/upload/)

## Installation

Keras and KerasHub can be installed with:

```
pip install -U -q keras-hub
pip install -U -q keras
```

JAX, TensorFlow, and Torch come pre-installed in Kaggle Notebooks. For instructions on installing them in another environment, see the [Keras Getting Started](https://keras.io/getting_started/) page.

## Presets

The following model checkpoints are provided by the Keras team. For each of the presets, we provide code examples in the tab below:

| Preset name                | Parameters | Description                                                          |
|----------------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `t5gemma2_270m_270m`       |   Total 370M (Shared Embeddings) |  Encoder–decoder (T5-style) Gemma model with 270M encoder + 270M decoder parameters, supporting text generation, multilingual tasks, and long-context inputs.   |
| `t5gemma2_1b_1b`       |    Total 1.4B (Shared Embeddings)|   Encoder–decoder (T5-style) Gemma model with 1B encoder + 1B decoder parameters, supporting text generation, multilingual tasks, and long-context inputs.  |
| `t5gemma2_4b_4b`       |  Total 5.6B (Shared Embeddings) |  Encoder–decoder (T5-style) Gemma model with 4B encoder + 4B decoder parameters, supporting text generation, multilingual tasks, and long-context inputs.  |

instances.usage:
```
import keras
import keras_hub
import numpy as np
```

Use `generate()` to do text generation, given an input context.

```
t5gemma2_lm = keras_hub.models.T5Gemma2Seq2SeqLM.from_preset("${VARIATION_SLUG}")
t5gemma_lm.generate("The quick brown fox", max_length=30)

# Generate with batched inputs.
t5gemma2_lm.generate(["The quick brown fox", "The whale"], max_length=30)
```

Compile the `generate()` function with a custom sampler.

```
t5gemma2_lm = keras_hub.models.T5Gemma2Seq2SeqLM.from_preset("${VARIATION_SLUG}")
t5gemma2_lm.compile(sampler="greedy")
t5gemma2_lm.generate("The quick brown fox", max_length=30)
```

Use `generate()` with encoder inputs and an incomplete decoder input (prompt).

```
t5gemma2_lm = keras_hub.models.T5Gemma2Seq2SeqLM.from_preset("${VARIATION_SLUG}")
t5gemma2_lm.generate(
    {
        "encoder_text": "The quick brown fox",
        "decoder_text": "The fast"
    }
)
```

# Model Summary
Data Format and Statistical Analysis
 * Sample Count: 40 samples using IDs formatted as attn_XXXX (sparse sampling of ~200 total, range 0001–0196).
 * Target: 7-dimensional vector per sample (float).
 * Prefix: attn_ → outputs from an attention mechanism.
Statistics per Dimension
| Dim | Min | Max | Mean | Std |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | -0.0636 | +0.0156 | -0.0200 | 0.0215 |
| 1 | -0.0925 | -0.0074 | -0.0544 | 0.0185 |
| 2 | -0.1886 | -0.0964 | -0.1482 | 0.0259 |
| 3 | -0.0414 | +0.0305 | +0.0002 | 0.0125 |
| 4 | -0.1204 | -0.0346 | -0.0838 | 0.0227 |
| 5 | -0.0169 | +0.0965 | +0.0354 | 0.0289 |
| 6 | -0.1596 | -0.0505 | -0.1065 | 0.0268 |
Analysis Summary
 * Global Range: [-0.1886, +0.0965] — Compressed signal, slightly negative centered (global mean: -0.054).
 * Dimension 2: Consistently negative and dominant — likely a track with higher cost or suppression.
 * Dimension 5: The only consistently positive dimension — constructive reinforcement.
 * Theoretical Alignment: This is consistent with the \Psi_n mechanism (where even n indicates reinforcement and odd n indicates suppression).


## Usage

The model is intended as a baseline submission for the ARC Prize Kaggle benchmark. It produces per-head embedding vectors that can be interpreted as a 7-track cognitive activation profile.

Load and predict example:
import pandas as pd
import ast

## Load submission output
df = pd.read_csv('submission.csv')
df['target'] = df['target'].apply(ast.literal_eval)

### Input shape:  (N,)  — string IDs of the form 'attn_XXXX'
### Output shape: (N, 7) — float32 vectors in range [-0.19, +0.10]
embeddings = pd.DataFrame(df['target'].tolist(), index=df['id'])

## System

The model is a standalone prediction module within the H7 Kaggle benchmark pipeline (github.com/jakobmina/h7-kaggle). Downstream, its 7-dim output feeds the dual Mahalanobis-Euclidean distance comparator for epsilon scoring per cognitive track.
    • Input: attention-head ID strings (attn_XXXX)
    • Output: 7-dim float vector per head
    • Downstream: H7 epsilon scoring, fairness audit engine, Intuition Index semaphore
entation requirements

What hardware and software were used for training the model? Describe the compute requirements for training and inference (e.g., # of chips, training time, total computation, measured performance, energy consumption).

**Implementation Requirements**

    • Software: Python 3.x, scikit-learn, pandas, numpy
    • Hardware: CPU-only — no GPU required for inference
    • Training compute: minimal (classical ML, no deep training loop)
    • Inference latency: sub-millisecond per sample on standard hardware

## Model Characteristics
## Model initialization

Trained from scratch using scikit-learn estimators. No pre-trained weights or transfer learning. The “double” prefix refers to a dual-pipeline architecture (two estimators whose outputs are combined or compared).
- Model Stats:

    • Output dimensionality: 7 (matches H7 Z₇ symmetry)
    • Effective output classes: 16 unique vectors (collapse from 40 samples)
    • Parameter count: lightweight — classical sklearn estimator weights only
    • Latency: < 1 ms per sample (CPU inference)
    • No neural layers, no attention heads, no transformer blocks

Other Details
    • No pruning or quantization applied
    • No differential privacy mechanisms
    • Output vectors are raw float predictions, not softmax-normalized
